channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Oil & Gas
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Equinor stops a four-day cyberattack on its IT systems with production untouched, as Skagerak Energi reports an attempted attack and Aker BP mobilises its emergency preparedness
item.description: Equinor, Norway’s state-controlled producer and one of Europe’s largest gas suppliers, disclosed on the evening of 17 November an ongoing attack on certain IT systems. Over the next two days it said the attack was not a virus and could not spread, that it did not appear to target Equinor specifically, and that it had been reported to the police; on 20 November it said the attack had been stopped. Throughout, Equinor says oil and gas production ran normally and it has found no sign that data was stolen or altered. A spokesperson told NTB that staff could have trouble using some corporate applications, and Reuters, citing an unnamed source, reported that internal email was down. Equinor has not said how the attackers got in, which systems were hit or who was behind it, and has given no timeline for full restoration. On 18 November utility Skagerak Energi reported an attempted attack on its IT systems with operations unaffected; Dark Reading reports that Aker BP mobilised its emergency preparedness and Statkraft said it was monitoring. There is no evidence the incidents are connected. Norway’s National Security Authority raised the national cyber risk level to four on a five-point scale in October, saying successful cyber operations against Norwegian organisations had tripled in six months. Nothing points to OT. The sector read is ours: an IT attack that leaves production running still tests whether the IT/OT boundary, remote access and the business systems operations depend on can be isolated and restored on their own. - Equinor statements (17 Nov 2026 18:55 CET; updates 18, 19 and 20 Nov 2026), reviewed directly; The Record (18 Nov 2026, NTB and Reuters details, NSM risk level); Rigzone (20 Nov 2026, Skagerak Energi); Dark Reading (Nov 2026, Aker BP and Statkraft); The Register (19 Nov 2026); oil and gas reading is editorial assessment - Disclosed 17 Nov 2026; declared stopped 20 Nov 2026; Skagerak Energi attempt reported 18 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Investigators suspect Iran behind the network breaches on two Texas-bound energy tankers, the Wall Street Journal reports, as Iran-linked hackers turn to physical effects
item.category: Incident — Network breaches aboard two Texas-bound energy tankers; investigators suspect Iran per the Wall Street Journal; no confirmed control of ship systems
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported on 12 November that investigators suspect Iran-linked hackers were behind three incidents since the summer: operators locked out of control panels at a small Midwestern water facility, hundreds of European supermarket refrigerators driven to about 49°C, and breached networks aboard two energy tankers in the Atlantic bound for Texas. The Coast Guard and FBI boarded two foreign-flagged vessels on 21 and 24 August; the Coast Guard reported no operational disruption, vessel instability or danger to crews, and in September US agencies were tracking threats to nearly 20 ships. The Iran link is a suspicion, not a formal attribution, and Iran denies involvement; Check Point linked the wider activity mainly to CyberAv3ngers. For marine terminals, the ship-shore interface is now a named target (editorial assessment). - Wall Street Journal (12 Nov 2026), as reported by Iran International (13 Nov 2026) and the Newsmax wire on Yahoo News (13 Nov 2026); Bloomberg via gCaptain (16 Sep 2026, boardings and ~20 ships tracked); attribution is investigators’ suspicion; terminal relevance is editorial assessment - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; WSJ report 12 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] Attackers rooted unpatched Check Point gateways through PHP2Shell, planted backdoors and wiped a VMware host; the root flaw is now in KEV
item.category: Incident — Exploitation of unpatched Check Point Mobile Access gateways; backdoors and a wiper on a VMware ESXi host; attribution unconfirmed; no OT victim reported
item.description: Check Point Research said on 12 November that attackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) on unpatched Check Point Mobile Access portals from 30 October, then used a local flaw, CVE-2026-123039, to become root. They deployed web shells and backdoors, moved to a VMware ESXi host over SSH and ran a wiper that zeroes files. The first wave hit Israeli organisations, some destructively; a second wave from 2 November reached several countries and sectors without destruction. Check Point cannot attribute it with confidence; the backdoors resemble tooling linked to China-nexus UNC5221. CISA added the root flaw to KEV on 13 November. No oil and gas victim is reported, but these gateways often front plant remote access and ESXi often hosts HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Check Point Research (12 Nov 2026), reviewed directly; CISA KEV alert (13 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1154 (12 Nov 2026, updated 13 Nov); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Wave 1 from 30 Oct 2026; wave 2 from 2 Nov 2026; research published 12 Nov 2026; KEV addition 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] N-able ships Hotfix 3 for 17 more N-central flaws after miners turned up on patched servers, then discloses a breach of its hosted email-filtering cloud
item.category: Incident — Exploitation of N-able N-central RMM servers (miners planted) and a separate breach of N-able’s hosted email-filtering cloud; no OT impact reported
item.description: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 3 on 16 November as a critical security update. It fixes 17 new CVEs, including authentication bypasses, path traversal leading to code execution and a syslog injection that runs commands as root, and removes the Legacy API option that the actively exploited 4EverAble2Shell chain depends on. It followed Huntback’s finding of cryptocurrency miners on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them already on Hotfix 2. On-premises servers need the upgrade now, and every customer must also upgrade Agents and Probes. Separately, N-able said on 20 November that attackers reached a server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud; it says mail flow continued, no access to customer data was found and N-central is unrelated. Integrators often manage plant-side Windows hosts through RMM tools (editorial assessment). - BleepingComputer (20 Nov 2026, Mail Assure/SpamExperts breach); The Hacker News (17 Nov 2026, Hotfix 3, citing N-able release notes of 16 Nov); The Hacker News (13 Nov 2026, citing Huntback); SecurityWeek (13 Nov 2026); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Mail Assure breach disclosed 20 Nov 2026; Hotfix 3 released 16 Nov 2026; exploitation reported 13 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] Cyberattack on Brazil’s Santos port authority forces manual workarounds at Latin America’s busiest port
item.category: Incident — Cyberattack on a port authority’s IT, access-control and coordination systems; manual workarounds; Latin America’s busiest port; terminal relevance is editorial
item.description: The Port of Santos authority, which runs Brazil’s largest port, lost its IT systems on 6 November and confirmed a cyberattack on 10 November. Access-control systems and digital tools for coordinating port operations went down, delaying vessel, truck and train procedures and forcing some checks, such as matching ship dimensions to berths, to be done by hand. By 16 November core internal systems were in final tests and about 70% of affected file backups had been recovered; ship movements and landside access continued throughout. Brazil’s Federal Police are investigating; the attacker and entry route are undisclosed. For fuel and liquid-bulk terminals inside a port, the lesson is to know how berthing and gate access work when the authority’s systems are down (editorial assessment). - The Rio Times (16 Nov 2026, status update citing the Santos Port Authority); DatamarNews (10 Nov 2026, updated 11 Nov); CyberDelegate (17 Nov 2026, citing Folha de S.Paulo, CNN Brasil and Agência Brasil); terminal relevance is editorial assessment - Outage from 6 Nov 2026; protection level raised 8 Nov; attack confirmed 10 Nov; ~70% of backups recovered by 16 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing

item.title: [Medium] DHS tells Congress Iran-backed hackers have stepped up attacks on US energy, water and transport since February, while officials rule out hacking in last week’s outages
item.category: Threat intelligence — US government testimony on Iranian targeting of US critical infrastructure incl. energy; no specific oil and gas incident named
item.description: In written testimony for a House Homeland Security Committee hearing on 18 November, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian state-sponsored groups and pro-Iranian criminals have targeted US critical infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began in February, with transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services increasingly in their sights. He described the attacks so far as mostly localised, low-damage disruptions of poorly secured industrial control systems, but warned that weak systems could have devastating consequences. At the same hearing, officials said they found no evidence that hackers caused the Microsoft 365 outage, the nationwide FAA ground stop or other recent disruptions. AttackIQ research released on 17 November describes Iranian groups passing network access to one another, often reaching targets through contractors and suppliers. For oil and gas, the weakest exposed controllers are the target (editorial assessment). - Jerusalem Post (18 Nov 2026, Mullin written testimony); Bloomberg (18 Nov 2026); Federal News Network (18 Nov 2026, outages not a coordinated attack); AttackIQ “Weighing Cyber Power”, via Water Online (17 Nov 2026); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Testimony and hearing 18 Nov 2026; AttackIQ research 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] FBI warns the ARTEX autonomous AI pentest framework is being used in real intrusions, some reaching privileged access in under three hours, with energy on the target list
item.category: Threat intelligence — FBI FLASH on malicious use of an autonomous AI penetration-testing framework; energy among targeted sectors; no oil and gas victim named
item.description: The FBI issued FLASH-20261113-001 on 13 November, warning that threat actors are using ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent penetration-testing framework written in Go, to automate reconnaissance, exploitation and exfiltration; some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours. ARTEX turns natural-language objectives into commands and plugs into outside AI models. Its developer pulled the GitHub repository on 8 October, but forks, mirrors and a commercial version keep it available, and researchers counted more than 1,600 exposed consoles in early November. The FBI lists energy among targeted sectors and names the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain compromise among ARTEX campaigns. Initial access comes through web-application flaws, weak or hard-coded credentials, abused vendor trust and stolen VPN configurations. Texas regulators cited the FLASH on 18 November (see Regulation & Policy). - FBI FLASH-20261113-001 (13 Nov 2026, TLP:CLEAR), reviewed directly; SC Media (Nov 2026); World Oil (18 Nov 2026, Texas RRC citing the FLASH); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - FLASH published 13 Nov 2026; activity since at least Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Dragos counts 47 ransomware attacks on oil and gas organisations in Q3 among 1,266 industrial cases, and saw no operator touching a control system
item.category: Research — Dragos quarterly industrial ransomware analysis; 47 oil and natural gas incidents in Q3 2026; no control-system manipulation observed
item.description: Dragos said on 16 November that ransomware hit 1,266 industrial organisations between July and September 2026, up 11% on the second quarter, and counted 47 oil and natural gas incidents across upstream, midstream, downstream and service providers. Among them, The Gentlemen listed Argentina’s Oldelval, which runs the main crude pipeline network out of Vaca Muerta, on 23 July; Oldelval said only administrative systems were affected and crude transport continued. Cl0p claimed Shell among its victims, a claim Dragos has not verified. Qilin and The Gentlemen led overall. Dragos saw no Q3 case of a ransomware operator manipulating a control system: disruption came through the IT, ERP and virtualisation layers plants depend on. Entry came through edge devices and enterprise applications exploited within days of disclosure, and through stolen VPN and firewall credentials. - Dragos Q3 2026 industrial ransomware analysis (16 Nov 2026), reviewed directly; Australian Cyber Security Magazine (17 Nov 2026) - Published 16 Nov 2026; data covers July–September 2026

item.title: [Medium] Trellix counts about 1,500 ransomware leak-site posts against industrial sectors in six months, up 50.8% quarter on quarter, and puts energy and oil and gas second in its OT telemetry
item.category: Research — Trellix OT Threat Report (Nov 2026, covering Apr–Sep 2026); mining and oil and gas extraction among tracked sectors; no control-system compromise reported
item.description: Trellix’s November OT Threat Report, covering April to September 2026, counts about 1,500 ransomware leak-site posts naming organisations in manufacturing, construction, transportation and warehousing, mining and oil and gas extraction, and utilities, up 50.8% quarter on quarter. Manufacturing accounts for about two-thirds and utilities under 2%; The Gentlemen and Qilin lead with about 16% each. In Trellix’s own product telemetry, energy and oil and gas make up 12.3% of OT-sector activity, second only to manufacturing at 49.3%; those shares measure product activity, not confirmed compromises. Trellix says the enterprise-edge exploitation it tracked did not establish a path into ICS networks. For oil and gas, the pressure stays on the IT and edge layers that production, scheduling and custody transfer depend on (editorial assessment). - Trellix Advanced Research Center, OT Threat Report November 2026 (page updated 12 Nov 2026); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Report published 12 Nov 2026; data covers April–September 2026

item.title: [Medium] Intel 471 finds access brokers sold entry to 172 manufacturing organisations this year, mostly through VPN and other perimeter remote access, from aerospace to chemicals
item.category: Research — Intel 471 analysis of ransomware and initial access brokers targeting manufacturing, aerospace through chemicals; cross-sector, editorial assessment for petrochemical and chemical units
item.description: Intel 471 said on 18 November that manufacturing was the most-targeted sector in its tracking from January to October 2026, with 1,379 ransomware and extortion claims, 16.8% of tracked victims. Initial access brokers offered access to 172 manufacturing entities, about 10% of all accesses offered, and 66.8% of those offers were wholesale. Perimeter remote access dominated, with VPN access at 28.5%. Intel 471 names Qilin, The Gentlemen and Akira among the groups active against the sector, and its report spans aerospace through chemicals. The figures are Intel 471’s own tracking and have not been independently verified. For petrochemical and chemical units and their suppliers, a sold VPN login is the likeliest first step toward a production outage (editorial assessment). - Intel 471 (18 Nov 2026), reviewed directly; Industrial Cyber (Nov 2026); petrochemical relevance is editorial assessment - Published 18 Nov 2026; data covers January–October 2026

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell: Schneider’s Foxboro DCS H90 Server still has no fix, and Siemens and ABB keep adding grid-control, RTU and gateway products
item.category: Active exploitation — PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) exploited against boundary firewalls; Schneider, Siemens and ABB list OT products incl. a Foxboro DCS server; several unfixed
item.description: Palo Alto’s Unit 42 verified research by Dream showing a suspected China-nexus actor chaining the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with Linux kernel bug CVE-2026-46300 to root about two dozen internet-exposed PAN-OS firewalls on 23–24 October and steal Active Directory credentials; Check Point gateways were later hit too (see Incidents & Attacks). OT vendors keep finding the same PHP code in their products. Schneider Electric lists the EcoStruxure Foxboro DCS H90 Server with no fix, mitigation only. Siemens lists Spectrum Power, AMIS TS and, since 16 November, WTV676/WTV776 metering gateways; ABB lists Netcontrol RTUs and ASPECT gateways, several unfixed. None of the OT products is reported exploited and no oil and gas operator is named. Foxboro DCS is widely used in refining and gas processing (editorial assessment). - Unit 42 (updated 29 Oct 2026); The Record (29 Oct 2026), citing Dream; Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v3.2.0 (30 Oct 2026); Siemens SSA-166980 V1.4 (16 Nov 2026); ABB Netcontrol and ASPECT advisories (29–30 Oct 2026); CISA KEV catalog; Foxboro relevance is editorial assessment - PHP fixes 21 Oct 2026; root compromises 23–24 Oct; KEV 26 and 28 Oct; Siemens metering gateways added 16 Nov 2026

item.title: [Critical] A vCenter authentication bypass was exploited as a zero-day for two months before Broadcom’s 19 November patch; vCenter 7.0 gets no fix
item.category: Active exploitation — VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 exploited as a zero-day by a suspected China-linked group; in KEV; no fix for vCenter 7.0
item.description: Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123890 on 19 November, a critical flaw in vCenter’s directory service that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker obtain an administrator session. Google’s Mandiant, which reported it, says a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited it for more than two months beforehand: it got in through a BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw, attacked vCenter in early September, stole SAML signing material and the vCenter master key, forged tokens and moved on to ESXi hosts. Fixes are in vCenter 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200 and 8.0 U3m; end-of-life vCenter 7.0 has no public patch. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 November. No victims or sectors are named. Many refineries and gas plants run HMIs, historians and engineering workstations as virtual machines, so whoever controls vCenter controls those hosts (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Broadcom and Google Threat Intelligence/Mandiant); CISA KEV alert (20 Nov 2026); The Hacker News (20–21 Nov 2026); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Exploited from at least early Sep 2026; patched 19 Nov 2026; added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Siemens: the Node2Shell Brotli flaw reaches WinCC, WinCC OA and TIA tools, and an NTLM relay weakness hits PCS 7 and Process Historian with no fix planned
item.category: Advisory — Siemens SSA-242944 (Brotli “Node2Shell” CVE-2026-111497, CVSS 9.8, in KEV) and SSA-970803 (NTLM relay CVE-2026-58114, CVSS 7.5) across WinCC, WinCC OA, PCS 7 and Process Historian; many without a fix
item.description: Siemens published two advisories on 10 November that CISA republished on 17 November. SSA-242944 (ICSA-26-321-03) covers CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli decoder buffer overflow behind October’s Node.js “Node2Shell” updates, scored CVSS 9.8: a crafted compressed stream can corrupt memory and potentially run code. Fixes exist for WinCC OA V3.20 (P17.1), Braumat and Sistar; WinCC V7/V8, WinCC OA V3.21, WinCC Unified, TIA Administrator and UMC have mitigations only. SSA-970803 (ICSA-26-321-08) describes an NTLM relay weakness, CVSS 7.5, that lets an on-path attacker impersonate users; no fix is planned for PCS 7 V9.1, Batch V9.1, Process Historian or Information Server, and none is available yet for WinCC. CISA added the Brotli CVE to KEV on 27 October. WinCC OA is common in pipeline SCADA and PCS 7 in refineries and petrochemical plants (editorial assessment). - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-242944 and SSA-970803 (10 Nov 2026), as republished by CISA in ICSA-26-321-03 and ICSA-26-321-08 (17 Nov 2026); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday (Nov 2026); CISA KEV catalog (Brotli addition 27 Oct 2026); sector usage is editorial assessment - Siemens advisories 10 Nov 2026; CISA republication 17 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Java4Shell exploitation attempts begin, and Siemens tells customers to take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.category: Advisory — OpenJDK Base64 memory-corruption flaw CVE-2026-114938 (“Java4Shell”); exploitation attempts; Siemens says take Industrial Edge Management offline until patched
item.description: Probing for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption bug in how OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later decode Base64 data, began within two days of its 17 November disclosure; GreyNoise counted more than 150 matching requests from five addresses by early 19 November, and none is confirmed to have succeeded. Exploitation needs a recent Intel or AMD processor with AVX-512 VBMI, and researchers at Calif showed unauthenticated code execution against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak setups. For OT teams the key item is Siemens SSA-272816: three Industrial Edge Management products are affected, fixes are in progress, and Siemens recommends taking those instances offline until patched. Cisco lists more than a dozen products with no fix yet, and Atlassian Data Center products are also unpatched. Engineering teams at plants often run Jira, Jenkins and Keycloak beside OT tooling (editorial assessment). - SecurityWeek (19 Nov 2026, citing Calif, GreyNoise, Previdian, Siemens SSA-272816, Cisco and Atlassian); The Record (18 Nov 2026, CISA alert); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Disclosed and patched 17 Nov 2026; exploitation attempts 18–19 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Attackers root clustered Cisco Expressway gateways soon after a public exploit, and CISA adds the flaw to KEV
item.category: Active exploitation — Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 in clustered Expressway Core and Edge; root on compromised nodes; in KEV
item.description: Security firm F6 says attackers exploited CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in clustered Cisco Expressway Core and Edge deployments, shortly after proof-of-concept code appeared on GitHub. They broke into two internet-facing Expressway nodes at an unnamed Russian organisation, moved to two more cluster nodes inside the network and gained root. From there they ran Python scripts, which F6 says show signs of AI-assisted writing, to scan for SMB shares, SQL Server and WinRM hosts and to search GitLab for credentials. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 November alongside the vCenter zero-day. Cisco disclosed and fixed it on 21 October; there is no workaround. No OT victim is reported, but Expressway is a perimeter gateway that bridges outside callers into internal networks, so an exposed, unpatched cluster is a foothold close to plant-side systems (editorial assessment). - Security Affairs (21 Nov 2026, CISA KEV additions of 20 Nov); SecurityWeek (Nov 2026, citing F6); Security Affairs (20 Nov 2026, F6 findings); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Patched 21 Oct 2026; exploitation reported 18–20 Nov 2026; added to CISA KEV 20 Nov 2026

item.title: [High] Fortinet publishes eight critical flaws in FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, including unauthenticated bugs in HA sync, BGP and the FGFM channel
item.category: Advisory — Eight critical Fortinet flaws (CVSS 9.0–9.8) in FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer and FortiSASE; no exploitation reported
item.description: Fortinet published eight critical advisories on 10 November across FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer and FortiSASE. Four are rated CVSS 9.8: a JSON RPC API encoding flaw, an SQL injection via OFTP and an FGFM authorisation flaw in FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, and missing authentication in FortiOS high-availability sync (CVE-2026-126259) when FGSP standalone-config-sync or autoscale is used. Others cover a BGP daemon truncation (9.6), an OSPF authentication bypass (9.3) and a pre-authentication SSRF over OFTP (9.0). Fixes are in FortiOS 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.8 and 8.0.2 and matching FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer builds, with some still listed as upcoming. No exploitation was reported and none is in KEV. FortiGate firewalls are common at refinery and pipeline IT/OT boundaries, and FortiBleed already harvested credentials for more than 86,000 devices (editorial assessment). - Fortinet PSIRT advisories (10 Nov 2026), as summarised by Daily CyberSecurity / SecurityOnline (10 Nov 2026); FortiBleed count per Dragos (16 Nov 2026); oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Published 10 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] Texas Railroad Commissioner urges oil, gas and pipeline operators to harden now, citing the FBI’s ARTEX warning and the recent wave of outages
item.category: Policy — State regulator call to action for Texas oil, gas and pipeline operators; no new rule
item.description: Railroad Commission of Texas Commissioner Wayne Christian again urged oil and gas producers, pipeline operators and other Texas energy companies on 18 November to bolster their cyber defences, saying the state’s energy infrastructure “is undoubtedly a target” and that operators cannot wait until an attack halts it. He pointed to the FBI’s 13 November FLASH on the ARTEX AI framework, which lists energy among targeted sectors (see Threat Intelligence & Research), and to recent widespread outages, while noting ARTEX may not be the only explanation; federal officials have said they found no evidence of hacking in those outages. He asked companies to find and fix vulnerabilities, secure their networks, monitor for suspicious activity and prepare a response plan before an attack. It is a call to action, not a new RRC rule. - World Oil (18 Nov 2026), citing the Railroad Commission of Texas; RRC press release (24 Sep 2026, earlier call and operator notice); FBI FLASH-20261113-001 (13 Nov 2026) - Statement reported 18 Nov 2026

item.title: [Info] France expects EU sanctions on 14 December against those behind October’s refrigeration sabotage, which Paris blames on an IRGC unit
item.category: Policy — Expected EU sanctions over Iran-attributed sabotage of refrigeration controllers; French attribution, denied by Iran; no direct oil and gas obligation
item.description: France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, said on 17 November that he expects EU foreign ministers to agree sanctions on 14 December against the individuals behind October’s sabotage of supermarket refrigeration controllers, freezing their assets and barring them from the EU, a day after EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said new Iran sanctions were being prepared. Paris blames the IRGC’s Shahid Kaveh unit for the attack on about 700 French sites, which French authorities say caused at least 15 fires, and has sought arrest warrants for three officers. Iran rejects the accusations, and the attribution has not been independently confirmed. For oil and gas, the case shows a state actor willing to cause physical effects through exposed industrial controllers, the same pattern suspected in the tanker breaches (see Incidents & Attacks; editorial assessment). - APA (18 Nov 2026, Barrot on France 5); Arab News, from AFP (17 Nov 2026, EU decision expected 14 Dec); dpa via Yahoo News (16 Nov 2026, Kallas); The Record (9 Nov 2026, French attribution and at least 15 fires); RFI via AOL (11 Nov 2026, warrant request) - Statements 16–18 Nov 2026; EU decision expected 14 Dec 2026
